papers.title: Diagnostic Image Quality of a Low-Field (0.55T) Knee MRI Protocol Using Deep Learning Image Reconstruction Compared with a Standard (1.5T) Knee MRI Protocol
papers.abstract: This study evaluates the image quality and diagnostic reliability of knee MRI performed at 0.55T using deep learning image reconstruction compared to standard 1.5T MRI. Twenty volunteers underwent knee MRI on both a 0.55T system (MAGNETOM Free.Max) and a 1.5T scanner (MAGNETOM Sola). Radiologists assessed overall image quality, noise, and diagnostic quality, finding that low-field MRI with deep learning reconstruction provides comparable diagnostic reliability to standard 1.5T MRI.

papers.title: Automatic Selection of Optimal TI for Flow-Independent Dark-Blood Delayed-Enhancement MRI
papers.abstract: This study proposes and evaluates an automatic approach for predicting the optimal inversion time (TI) for dark and gray blood images in flow-independent dark-blood delayed-enhancement (FIDDLE) MRI. Data from 267 patients were acquired on 3T MAGNETOM Vida and 1.5T MAGNETOM Sola scanners. The method reliably predicted optimal TIs with an average error of less than 10 ms compared to manual annotations, enhancing the efficiency of FIDDLE acquisitions.

papers.title: Next-Generation MRI Scanner Designed for Ultra-High-Resolution Human Brain Imaging at 7 Tesla
papers.abstract: To enhance human neuroimaging, a next-generation 7 Tesla MRI scanner was developed, featuring an asymmetric gradient coil and a 128-channel receiver system. This design enables functional imaging studies at 0.35-0.45 mm isotropic resolution, revealing cortical layer activity and improving diffusion imaging. The scanner achieves high angular resolution and reduces acquisition time for both functional and structural imaging.

papers.title: Impact of Non-Contrast-Enhanced Imaging Input Sequences on the Generation of Virtual Contrast-Enhanced Breast MRI Scans Using Neural Network
papers.abstract: This study investigates the impact of non-contrast-enhanced imaging input sequences on generating virtual contrast-enhanced breast MRI scans using a neural network. The cohort included patients who underwent diagnostic breast MRI on 3T scanners (MAGNETOM Skyra-Fit or MAGNETOM Vida). The findings suggest that specific non-contrast sequences can effectively generate virtual contrast-enhanced images, potentially reducing the need for contrast agents.

papers.title: Magnetic Resonance Imaging in Patients with Cardiac Implantable Electronic Devices: The RESONANCE Spanish Registry
papers.abstract: The RESONANCE Spanish Registry evaluates the safety and feasibility of performing MRI in patients with cardiac implantable electronic devices (CIEDs). The study includes data from multiple centers, assessing protocols and outcomes of MRI scans conducted on patients with CIEDs. The findings support the safe integration of MRI into clinical practice for this patient population.

Indications for Use (Describe)
Indications for Use for MAGNETOM Vida, MAGNETOM Lumina, MAGNETOM Vida Fit, MAGNETOM Sola,
MAGNETOM Altea, MAGNETOM Sola Fit, MAGNETOM Viato.Mobile:
The MAGNETOM system is indicated for use as a magnetic resonance diagnostic device (MRDD) that produces
transverse, sagittal, coronal and oblique cross sectional images, spectroscopic images and/or spectra, and that displays the
internal structure and/or function of the head, body, or extremities. Other physical parameters derived from the images
and/or spectra may also be produced. Depending on the region of interest, contrast agents may be used. These images
and/or spectra and the physical parameters derived from the images and/or spectra when interpreted by a trained physician
yield information that may assist in diagnosis.
The MAGNETOM system may also be used for imaging during interventional procedures when performed with MR
compatible devices such as in-room displays and MR Safe biopsy needles.

Indications for Use for MAGNETOM Flow.Elite, MAGNETOM Flow.Neo, MAGNETOM Flow.Rise:
The MAGNETOM system is indicated for use as a magnetic resonance diagnostic device (MRDD) that produces
transverse, sagittal, coronal and oblique cross sectional images, spectroscopic images and/or spectra, and that displays,
depending on optional local coils that have been configured with the system, the internal structure and/or function of the
head, body, or extremities. Other physical parameters derived from the images and/or spectra may also be produced.
Depending on the region of interest, contrast agents may be used. These images and/or spectra and the physical
parameters derived from the images and/or spectra when interpreted by a trained physician yield information that may
assist in diagnosis.
The MAGNETOM system may also be used for imaging during interventional procedures when performed with MR
compatible devices such as in-room displays and MR Safe biopsy needles.
